Vs.

full_judgment: 10. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions of the learned Advocates for both sides. It is clear from the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge that he has made certain surmises in course of his judgment. His surmises have no basis. These are with regard to the payment of rent on the basis of Ext. A and also with regard to heirs and female co-sharers possessing their ancestral land. The learned Additional District Judge has also not adverted to certain important aspects of the case considered by the learned trial Court. In particular, he has not adverted to the fact that Defdt. No. 1 Abdus Sattar, the father-in-law of Sayed Moula Ali himself had written the kabala Ext. 2C which shows transfer of khas land and not of superior interest. The learned Additional District Judge has also not sufficiently explained the absence of Dakhila and Patta in pursuance of Ext A, but the absence of those documents had weighed with the learned Subordinate Judge who tried the suit. In these circumstances. I am of the opinion that the appellate Court's judgment was not a proper judgment of reversal.
